frames.narration: The error rate of the checkout service jumps from 0.4% to 9%. The rule says: error rate above 5% for 2 minutes. The evaluator runs it every 30 seconds. The first evaluation sees 9%, but the condition has not held for 2 minutes yet, so the alert is only pending.

Four evaluations later, 2 minutes after the first, the rate is still above 5%, so the alert fires. All 12 checkout pods report the problem, so the evaluator sends 12 alerts with the same service and alertname labels and a different pod label.

The alert manager checks its silences: the only one covers the batch service, so nothing matches. It then merges repeats by fingerprint, since the evaluator will send the same 12 alerts again every 30 seconds, and groups them by service and alertname. After a 30 second group wait there is one group of 12 alerts.
The router matches service=checkout and severity=critical to the payments team's route, which pages. It asks the schedule who is on call, and gets Dana as primary and Sam as secondary.

The router writes a page for Dana to the queue with an idempotency key, so a retry cannot create a second page. The notifier sends a push notification and a text message, and the router starts a 5 minute acknowledgement timer.

Dana's phone is in a tunnel and the message does not arrive. Five minutes pass with no acknowledgement. The timer expires, and the escalation policy pages the secondary, Sam, using a push and a phone call.

Sam acknowledges the page. The router stops the escalation timer. The group stays open, so a new alert for checkout joins it without paging again. The acknowledgement and the delay of 5 minutes are recorded in the incident history.
Sam rolls back the bad release and the error rate falls below 5%. The evaluator marks the 12 alerts resolved, the manager closes the group, and one resolved message goes to the people who were paged.
